headings.title: SMTO-POL-0010 — SMTO can't use the computer this step asked for

html:
SMTO-POL-0010 — SMTO can't use the computer this step asked for

GUID: ee92aa2d-beb3-4c2c-8221-9b51e1b3cf2d
Slug: target-scope-invalid
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • A step tried to run on, or copy files between, Gateways (the helper programs SMTO uses on your computers) that aren't selected for this task, aren't available now, or can't do that. The step did not run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select the Gateway button next to the message box and check that every computer the task needs is selected (up to 16). A task can only use the Gateways that were selected when it started.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and make sure those Gateways are enabled and connected. A Gateway that is offline, disabled or has been set up again can't be used by a task that started earlier.
  3. To copy files on one computer, ask for a normal copy on that computer. To copy between two computers, select both and make sure both support file transfer. SMTO uses different copy actions for one computer and for two, and refuses the wrong one.
  4. Send your request again as a new message. A new task picks up the Gateways you have selected now.

What success looks like

  • The step runs and shows the expected Gateway name, or 'source → destination' for a copy.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the names of the computers you selected, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't remove and re-add a Gateway while a task is still using it; that task will refuse the changed Gateway.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway target validation raised TargetScopeError: the target was malformed, outside the run's captured Gateway selection, unavailable or disabled, lacked file_transfer, changed identity since capture, or a cross-Gateway copy named the same Gateway as source and destination.

What this means

  • Gateway target validation rejects malformed, uncaptured, unavailable, identity-changed or unsupported transfer targets, including a cross-Gateway flow used for a same-Gateway copy. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway target validation rejects malformed, uncaptured, unavailable, identity-changed or unsupported transfer targets, including a cross-Gateway flow used for a same-Gateway copy.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare target identity, captured scope, availability and transfer capability; use the same-Gateway file-copy flow when both ends are the same target.

How to fix it

  • Read the TargetScopeError text in the operation result. Check the run's captured gateway_selection and target contexts (gateways/tool_scope.py selected_targets), each Gateway record's enabled flag and identity fields, and file_transfer support (skills/gateway/copy_preflight.py); use file.copy with target for a same-Gateway copy, and start a new request after changing the selection.
  • Select the intended permitted target and refresh its current scope; keep target authorization intact.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Both selected endpoints pass the intended operation's current identity and scope checks.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
